skill.name: hypothesis-generation
skill.description: Generate testable scientific hypotheses from observations, literature, and competing explanations, then design experiments and predictions to evaluate them.
skill.summary: Create evidence-based hypotheses, predictions, and experimental test plans for scientific research.
skill.author: davila7

content.value_statement: Researchers often need structured hypotheses that connect observations, evidence, and experiments. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through literature search, competing explanations, predictions, and report formatting.
actual_capabilities: Turns observations or research questions into 3 to 5 competing scientific hypotheses.
Guides literature search strategy for PubMed and broader scientific web sources.
Evaluates hypotheses using testability, falsifiability, parsimony, scope, and explanatory power.
Designs experiments, controls, measurements, and predictions for each hypothesis.
Structures a concise LaTeX-style hypothesis report with appendices and citations.
Provides formatting guidance for colored hypothesis, prediction, evidence, and summary boxes.
limitations: It does not replace expert review, ethics approval, or statistical consultation.
It depends on available literature and may miss paywalled or unpublished evidence.
It can propose experiments but cannot validate feasibility, cost, or safety by itself.
LaTeX compilation and figure generation require local tools or separate approved workflows.

use_cases.title: Plan a Mechanistic Study
use_cases.description: Develop competing mechanisms, predictions, controls, and measurements for a biological or physical phenomenon.

use_cases.title: Convert Observations Into Research Questions
use_cases.description: Turn preliminary results into evidence-based hypotheses that can guide the next round of experiments.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Hypothesis Report
use_cases.description: Create a structured report with concise main findings, detailed appendices, citations, and experiment plans.

prompt_templates.title: Generate Initial Hypotheses
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the hypothesis-generation skill to propose testable hypotheses for this observation: [describe observation]. Include the main assumptions and one prediction for each hypothesis.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Competing Explanations
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the hypothesis-generation skill to create 3 to 5 competing mechanistic hypotheses for [phenomenon]. Compare their evidence, assumptions, and falsifiable predictions.

prompt_templates.title: Design Experiments
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the hypothesis-generation skill to design experiments that distinguish between these hypotheses: [list hypotheses]. Include controls, measurements, expected results, and confounds.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Full Research Report
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced report generation with literature and formatting.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the hypothesis-generation skill to prepare a structured hypothesis report for [research question]. Include literature search strategy, hypotheses, predictions, experimental designs, and appendix content.

output_examples.input: Why does treatment response vary between two patient subgroups?
output: Three competing hypotheses covering biomarker expression, immune microenvironment, and pharmacokinetic differences.
Predictions that distinguish each explanation using measurable subgroup outcomes.
Experimental designs with controls, sample considerations, and likely confounds.

output_examples.input: Generate hypotheses for an unexpected decrease in material strength after processing.
output: Mechanistic explanations involving microstructure, thermal history, contamination, and measurement artifacts.
A comparison plan using microscopy, composition analysis, process controls, and repeat testing.
A concise report structure with main hypotheses and detailed appendix sections.

best_practices: Provide the observation, domain, known constraints, and any preliminary data before asking for hypotheses.
Ask for competing hypotheses, not only the most likely explanation.
Review proposed experiments with domain experts before using resources or involving participants.
anti_patterns: Do not treat generated hypotheses as established scientific facts.
Do not skip literature search when evidence is needed to support a mechanism.
Do not request only confirmatory evidence for a preferred hypothesis.

faq.question: What does this skill produce?
faq.answer: It produces competing hypotheses, supporting evidence, testable predictions, experiment plans, and structured report guidance.

faq.question: Can it search scientific literature?
faq.answer: It guides literature search strategy and can use available web tools when the host environment provides them.

faq.question: Does it work outside biomedical research?
faq.answer: Yes. The framework can support physical sciences, engineering, social science, and interdisciplinary research questions.

faq.question: Can it create publication-ready reports?
faq.answer: It provides LaTeX-oriented structure and formatting guidance, but final review, citations, and compilation remain the user responsibility.

faq.question: How many hypotheses should I request?
faq.answer: The skill recommends 3 to 5 distinct hypotheses so experiments can compare plausible explanations.

faq.question: Is this a substitute for expert scientific judgment?
faq.answer: No. It is a planning aid that should be checked by qualified researchers and relevant review processes.
